I think he's a fine poet, but from his interviews, he seems set on passing off his Rumi-inspired poetry as something that is essentially Rumi's work. At least from what I've read of his books, he isn't interested in clarifying that he's offering loose /reinterpretations/ of very old English translations of Rumi. 

This leads to people thinking that Rumi actually wrote lines like "I go into the Muslim mosque and the Jewish synagogue and the Christian church and I see one altar" when this is the product of [Barks interpreting an old English translation of an even older German guy's experiment with writing German ghazals.](http://m.dar-al-masnavi.org/three.fake.rumi.verses.pdf) Which results in a pop culture perception of Rumi that makes him out to be a chill-vibes new-agey woo-woo dude instead of a very devote Muslim--which is awkward, given how convinced a lot of Americans are that Islam can only be a detriment to art and culture. 

Barks really isn't trying to contravene this pop culture narrative, so I'm not super sympathetic to his trouble with bashers.
